thread:
anya: Quick sync — canary profiling shows tail latency spike when KV hit ratio < ~65%. I think kernel selection + admission/pacing are interacting awkwardly. Anyone free to brainstorm SLA-aware pacing and queue tweaks?
max: I pulled traces, flamegraphs look like long GC-ish tails but root cause seems waiting on KV fetchs then kernel fallback. Pasted a short excerpt below.
devon: yeah, saw it too. When prefix cache misses, we end up doing an extra KV roundtrip and then the runtime picks fallback matmul kernels (slow GEMM path) — batches still grow while those requests block.
oliver: do we have samples showing whether the slow kernel is the quantized path or a memcpy stall?
max: snippet from perf agent:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:04Z canary-42 trace: batch_size=16 wait_for_kv=23ms kv_hit_ratio=0.61 kernel=matmul_slow latency_p50=22ms p95=142ms p99=320ms
2026-03-15T10:12:04Z canary-42 worker0: kernel_switch_reason=kv_miss probe_time=18ms
```
devon: that's consistent. My hypothesis: admission allows large batch formation based on queued tokens, but if many are kv-miss the effective compute per-request increases and we push a slower kernel and then tail explodes.
anya: proposal: make admission consider a short-term KV hit signal and enforce a tighter token_budget_target + enabled pacing when signal < threshold. e.g. if kv_hit_ratio < 0.7 -> token_budget_target := 30% lower, max_batch_time_ms := 6, enable_sla_pacing := true.
max: ran a quick A/B: pacing=true, kv-aware admit on canary-43 -> p99 down ~18ms, throughput -6%. Logs: 
```
canary-43 A: kv_hit=0.82 p99=128ms tput=980rps
canary-43 B: kv_hit=0.58 p99=110ms tput=920rps (pacing on)
```
devon: tradeoff looks reasonable for latency-sensitive routes. For best-effort we should keep current aggressive batching. We need a per-route policy.
oliver: also consider a probe-kernel step: when batch forms, run a tiny synthetic forward on first token (cheap micro-batch) to pick kernel path/quantization preference. If slow path chosen, shrink the batch early and admit fewer tokens. Might add overhead but reduces massive tail.
anya: +1. Implementation idea: during batch formation, after the first request arrives and before waiting full batch_time, kick a 'kernel-probe' that records kernel signal. If probe indicates fallback, set local batch_max_size = max(2, floor(batch_max_size/2)).
max: caution: client-side retries will amplify 429s. If we move to stricter rejects under low-kv and high-queue, ensure Retry-After header and a small jitter/backoff guidance.
devon: agree. Also prefer graceful shedding: prefer rejecting low-priority or long-token requests first (priority hint from header). If we must 429, prefer marking as "evict-first" not random.
anya: example admit policy patch I sketched:
```yaml
admission:
  token_budget_target: 38  # baseline
  max_batch_time_ms: 8
  kv_aware:
    enabled: true
    window_ms: 3000
    threshold: 0.7
    token_budget_multiplier_when_low: 0.65
  pacing:
    enabled: true
    probe_kernel: true
    probe_timeout_ms: 2
```
oliver: we should also surface these signals in Console (per-route kv_hit ratio + kernel_switch rate) so oncall can flip policy per-route quickly.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary-43 -> canary-46. Rolling update at 11:15 UTC. CI: perf-tests + kv-sim passed. :rocket:
max: ok let's run targeted canaries for three routes (chat-low-latency, chat-bg, embed-high-throughput). I'll deploy patch with probe off for embed-high-throughput initially.
anya: can we add automated alert if probe_kernel_switch_rate > 5% and p99 increases by >30ms in 5m window?
devon: yes. I'll add an eval hook that emits an event to perf-alerts.
oliver: follow-up: schedule 30min sync after canary results. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
